test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 12 Nov 2021 Shift 2
subject: general
question:
**Select the correct indirect narration of the given sentence.**

“Oh! I’ve missed the deadline for sending my application again,” Nidhi said.

options.text: Nidhi is exclaiming in disappointment that she had missed the deadline for sending her application again.
Nidhi exclaimed because she has missed the deadline for sending her application again.
Nidhi exclaimed in disappointment that she had missed the deadline for sending her application again.
Nidhi exclaimed in disappointment that she was missing the deadline for sending her application again.

solution:
The correct answer is: **Nidhi exclaimed in disappointment that she had missed the deadline for sending her application again.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and we need to convert it to **in****direct **speech.
 
• When we change a direct speech to indirect speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• An exclamatory sentence has a sign of exclamation after it which changes into a full stop in the indirect speech.
 
• The "full stop" in the indirect speech changes to Exclamation Point ( ! ) in the direct speech.
 
• The reporting verb '**said**' changes to 'exclaimed' in the reported speech part.
 
• To express the exclamatory phrase, "What! Oh! How!" are used. (**Oh**! express **disappointment**)
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the conjunction 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is removed to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The first word of the indirect speech is in capital letter.
 
• If the direct speech is written in the **present perfect tense**, then we have to change it to the **past perfect tense** in indirect speech. therefore **"have missed" **becomes **"had missed"** to show the indirect speech.
 
• "**I**" in direct speech becomes "**she**" in indirect speech according to gender.
 
• "**my**" in direct speech becomes "**her**" in indirect speech according to gender.
 
 

Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

Hence, direct speech is - *Nidhi exclaimed in disappointment that she had missed the deadline for sending her application again.*
